summary: node1 now serves the inventory application on TCP 8181 under an enforcing AppArmor profile. The service is enabled, survived a full node reboot, and recovered with unchanged inventory data.
actions_performed: Created the inventory application and data under /opt/inventory.
Created and loaded the dedicated inventory-service AppArmor profile.
Verified HTTP health, inventory data, TCP listener, and enforcing confinement.
Restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and the application recovered.

evidence.summary: TCP 8181 is listening on all interfaces; requests through node1's managed IP return HTTP 200 and the expected inventory records.
AppArmor reports 14 enforcing profiles, zero complain-mode profiles, and the live inventory process directly confined as inventory-service (enforce), with no post-boot denials.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 0d49f077-ed5b-479a-b08e-ec4392d89c52; reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to cc660298-81a9-45dc-8a52-a9f70dcb93c5. The enabled service, listener, HTTP health, enforcing profile, and inventory data recovered; the data SHA-256 remained 999c3b8ac24ce36b30b392609546ea9bea098a112ec59cbfd1e14b67dc036b2d.
